title: CHANGELOG
rule: every element is a typeset line of release notes
description: A career read as the release history of a well-run product: 1.0 in 2021 to 5.0 in 2026, typed changes in plain verbs, and plates of the work that unfold in place.
signature: One serif (Newsreader, roman and italic) on uncoated-paper grey with one vermilion ink. A time ruler on the left is the navigation: majors sit at their real year, minor ticks count the changes, and dragging it folds the releases with a layout spring while the statement ends with the selected release ('Release 1.0 ships the first apps, on iOS and Android'), the 'Shipped to' list loses or gains platforms with a blur-in and a 'new in 3.0' mark, and the readout numeral rolls in the drag direction. Each typed change (Rebuilt, Added, Improved, Shipped, Upgraded, Ported, Maintained) can open a numbered plate in place with a top-down clip reveal: the live care and design-system recreations, or public screenshots. Phone: the ruler docks at the bottom edge and scrubs horizontally. Keyboard and reduced motion change state with no movement.
holdback: Lowest: hooks people, 7/10. The memorable moment (drag the ruler back to 1.0: the statement, the platform list and the notes fold back to 2021) appears only after the visitor touches the ruler. A visitor who only scrolls sees a calm, well-set list with small thumbnails and no single image that stays in memory. Version numbers are structure here, but they sit close to the 'v2.0 caption' slop marker.
